gloss: on the small side; somewhat less; light (portion)

definitions.gloss: on the small side; somewhat less; a smaller amount
definitions.explanation: Indicates a quantity that is slightly less than normal or standard. Often used when requesting or describing portions of food, drink, or other quantities.

examples.japanese: ごはんは{少|すく}なめでお{願|ねが}いします。
examples.english: A smaller portion of rice, please.

examples.japanese: {塩|しお}は{少|すく}なめにしたほうがいい。
{今月|こんげつ}は{出費|しゅっぴ}を{少|すく}なめに{抑|おさ}えたい。
examples.english: I want to keep expenses on the lower side this month.

notes:
Formed from {少|すく}ない + the suffix め (tending toward, slightly). Indicates a quantity slightly less than normal.

WORD FORMATION:
{少|すく}ない (few, little) + め (suffix: -ish, somewhat). This pattern is productive:
- {多|おお}め: on the larger side (opposite)
- {大|おお}きめ: slightly larger
- {小|ちい}さめ: slightly smaller
- {長|なが}め: slightly longer
- {短|みじか}め: slightly shorter

COMMON USES:
- ごはん{少|すく}なめ: less rice (when ordering)
- {油|あぶら}{少|すく}なめ: less oil
- {塩|しお}{少|すく}なめ: less salt

USAGE:
Very common when ordering food at restaurants. Often seen on ramen shop order forms. Can also describe quantities in general: {出費|しゅっぴ}を{少|すく}なめに{抑|おさ}える (keep expenses on the low side).
